URL: https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2026/09/30/nato-russia-nuclear-kaliningrad-hybrid-sabotage/8101f542-bcef-11f1-81fc-9b76f8343b6c_story.html
The Washington Post (Lorne Cook, Associated Press) — published 30 September 2026, dateline BRUSSELS

Russia has warned NATO that it would not hesitate to use nuclear weapons to defend Kaliningrad should any members of the military bloc try to cut off its western exclave from the rest of the country.
(Retrieved excerpt is the top of the story only — the rest is behind the paywall for this session. Verify any further detail directly.)

CORROBORATING DETAIL FROM NON-APPROVED CARRIERS — flagged, do not use unattributed:
- The non-paper's text, "seen by Reuters": Moscow accused the alliance of pursuing a "dangerous and reckless course" carrying "high risks of the outbreak of a direct armed conflict"; warned any confrontation could include Russian strikes against decision-making centres in NATO member states from the beginning of a conflict; and said "Russia will be ready to use the entire arsenal of forces and capabilities at its disposal, including nuclear weapons" if NATO countries attempted to isolate Kaliningrad. (Seen via moderndiplomacy.eu — NOT approved. The underlying Reuters copy should be on reuters.com.)
- NATO spokesperson Allison Hart: "I can confirm that Russia sent a non-paper to NATO and that we have sent a response, noting that NATO is a defensive Alliance and none of our activities or exercises pose a risk to any part of Russia." / "We strongly denounce the threat of force, including any irresponsible nuclear rhetoric." / "Russia's use of hybrid tactics is a sign of desperation. But we will not be dissuaded from our support to Ukraine. We have what it takes to defend every inch of Allied territory and remain strong, ready and able to counter any threat." (Seen via rapporteur.com, pravda.com.ua, theepochtimes.com — none approved. nato.int IS approved: check there for the spokesperson's briefing.)
- Russian embassy in London, Telegram, 29 Sep: "Those advocating plans to blockade Kaliningrad or launch a strike against it should have no illusions about the consequences. Any military action by the UK or NATO against Russian territory will be met with a response using all means available to Russia, including nuclear weapons." (Seen via tass.com and aa.com.tr — NOT approved. TASS is a Russian state outlet.)
- Lithuania described Russia's new threats over Kaliningrad as psychological pressure (via pravda.com.ua — not approved).
- Reuters has published an explainer, "Why Russia's Kaliningrad is a potential flashpoint with NATO", listed on https://www.reuters.com/world/ — URL not captured.
